### Block 1 — Bring in Dependabot PR #7 (lodash 4.17.21)

- **Goal:** lodash resolves to 4.17.21 on the working branch, with the same change Dependabot proposed in PR #7.
- **Closes:** [dependabot#2](https://github.com/acme-telco/portal-web/security/dependabot/2), GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm, CVE-2021-23337
- **Priority:** P1 (highest score 75)
- **Steps:**
  1. Re-check the PR: `gh pr view 7 --json state,mergeable,statusCheckRollup,headRefName`.
  2. `git fetch origin dependabot/npm_and_yarn/lodash-4.17.21`
  3. `git log --oneline "$(git merge-base HEAD FETCH_HEAD)"..FETCH_HEAD` (expect Dependabot's commit only).
  4. `git cherry-pick --no-commit <sha>`, then one commit for the block, noting "supersedes Dependabot PR #7". The PR is never merged with `gh pr merge`. GitHub closes it as superseded once you integrate the branch.
- **Fix-risk:** low
  - patch jump 4.17.20 → 4.17.21
  - transitive dependency, lockfile-only change (`package-lock.json`)
  - Dependabot PR #7 is healthy: MERGEABLE, checks SUCCESS
- **Effort:** S (under an hour)
- **Verification:** `npm ci && npm test -- --watch=false && npm run build`
- **Who acts:** agent (mechanical)
- **Depends on:** —

### Block 2 — Angular framework patch 11.0.0 → 11.0.5

- **Goal:** every `@angular/*` framework package is on 11.0.5, the first patched version.
- **Closes:** [dependabot#1](https://github.com/acme-telco/portal-web/security/dependabot/1), GHSA-c75v-2vq8-873c, CVE-2021-4231
- **Priority:** P1 (highest score 70)
- **Steps:**
  1. `npx --no-install ng update @angular/core@11.0.5 @angular/cli@11.0.5` (the framework packages move together; asked before running, because it installs packages).
  2. `git diff --stat` (expect `package.json` and `package-lock.json` only).
- **Fix-risk:** low
  - patch within the same major (11.0.0 → 11.0.5)
  - direct dependency; `@angular/common`, `@angular/compiler`, `@angular/forms`, `@angular/router` and the other framework packages move with `@angular/core`, never `@angular/core` alone
  - only manifests and the lockfile change
  - Karma suite present (`npm test`); the baseline is recorded before block 1
- **Effort:** S (under an hour)
- **Verification:** `npm ci && npx --no-install ng build && npx --no-install ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`
- **Who acts:** agent (mechanical)
- **Depends on:** —

### Block 3 — Fix client-side XSS in `src/app/render.ts`

- **Goal:** the value written at `src/app/render.ts:42` goes through Angular's sanitization, and CodeQL no longer reports `js/xss` there.
- **Closes:** [code-scanning#1](https://github.com/acme-telco/portal-web/security/code-scanning/1) (`js/xss`, Client-side cross-site scripting)
- **Priority:** P2 (highest score 40)
- **Steps:**
  1. Read `src/app/render.ts` around line 42 and trace where the rendered value comes from.
  2. Propose the change as a diff (for example, bind it through Angular's template sanitization, or `DomSanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, …)`, instead of writing raw HTML). It is applied only after you approve it.
  3. Add or extend a unit test that pins the escaped output.
- **Fix-risk:** low
  - local change in one function of one application file
  - behaviour preserved for safe input; a unit test can pin it
  - Copilot Autofix is unavailable for this alert, so the fix is written by hand
- **Effort:** S (under an hour)
- **Verification:** `npx --no-install ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless && npx --no-install ng build`. CodeQL closes the alert after the next analysis of `main`.
- **Who acts:** agent (prepares the change and applies it once approved), developer (approves it)
- **Depends on:** —

### Block 4 — karma 5.1 → 6.3.16 (major upgrade of the test runner)

- **Goal:** karma is on 6.3.16, the first patched version, and the test suite still runs.
- **Closes:** [dependabot#3](https://github.com/acme-telco/portal-web/security/dependabot/3) (karma), GHSA-7x7c-qm48-pq9c, CVE-2022-0437
- **Priority:** P3 (highest score 25)
- **Steps:**
  1. `npm ls karma`, then read `peerDependencies.karma` in `node_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular/package.json` to confirm that the installed Angular builder accepts karma 6. If it does not, stop and tell you: the alert then moves to "Will not be fixed now", or you choose block 5.
  2. `npm install --save-dev karma@6.3.16` (asked before running, because it installs packages).
  3. Align the karma plugins (`karma-jasmine`, `karma-chrome-launcher`, `karma-coverage`) only if their peer ranges require it. Change `karma.conf.js` only if karma 6 rejects it, and show you that edit first.
- **Fix-risk:** high
  - major jump of karma itself, 5.1 → 6.3.16
  - direct `development` dependency: nothing in the production build changes
  - `karma.conf.js` may need changes (a config file)
  - the upgrade changes the test runner itself, so a failure shows up as a suite that does not start; the baseline is recorded before block 1
- **Effort:** M (up to half a day)
- **Verification:** `npm ci && npx --no-install ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless && npx --no-install ng build`
- **Who acts:** agent (mechanical bump), developer (approves any `karma.conf.js` edit)
- **Depends on:** —

## Illustrative: how an Angular major-upgrade block looks (not derived from this repo's alerts)

This repo's open Angular alert is fixed by a patch inside major 11 (block 2), so this plan has no Angular major hop. The block below is not part of the plan. It only shows the format the skill uses when an alert's first patched version is in the next Angular major. The alert, versions and factors are hypothetical. Every major hop (11 → 12, 12 → 13, …) is its own block, never mixed with routine bumps.

### Block N — Angular 11 → 12

- **Goal:** the app builds and its tests pass on Angular 12, which closes the `@angular/*` alert patched in 12.x.
- **Closes:** a hypothetical `@angular/*` alert whose first patched version is 12.x (in a real plan: the alert link and its GHSA/CVE ids)
- **Priority:** copied from the scripts for that alert (in a real plan: the band and the highest score)
- **Steps:**
  1. `git status --porcelain` (must be empty), then `npx --no-install ng update` to list what can move (it changes nothing).
  2. `npx --no-install ng update @angular/core@12 @angular/cli@12` (asked before running; it runs the 11 → 12 migrations).
  3. `npx --no-install ng update @angular/material@12 @angular/cdk@12` (when Angular Material is used).
  4. Update each third-party Angular library to its release for Angular 12.
  5. Build and test. Every compile fix in application code is shown to you as a diff and needs your approval.
- **Fix-risk:** high (always, for an Angular major hop)
  - major hop 11 → 12, a single hop (a fix in 13.x would need a second block, 12 → 13)
  - TypeScript 4.0 → 4.2: `typescript` must be in the range Angular 12 supports (`https://angular.dev/reference/versions`)
  - `@angular/material` and `@angular/cdk` move to 12 with `@angular/core` (same major)
  - Node.js: `engines.node`, `.nvmrc` and the CI image must be in the range Angular 12 supports; a CI image change happens outside the repo
  - third-party Angular libraries (`ngx-*`, `@ngrx/*`, …): each needs a release for Angular 12, and a library without one blocks the hop
  - the breaking changes from the 11.0 → 12.0 update guide that apply to this repo, each with its evidence (for example, `ng build` uses the production configuration by default from 12)
  - number of application files to change, and the tests available to catch regressions
- **Effort:** L (a day or more); M for a small app with few third-party libraries
- **Verification:** `npm ci && npx --no-install ng build && npx --no-install ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`
- **Who acts:** agent (runs `ng update` after approval), developer (approves every code edit), human outside the repo (if the CI image's Node.js must change)
- **Depends on:** the blocks that must land first, if any
